identity.operation: Report an object-member type error during json_vunpack_ex.
identity.condition: A keyed member has the wrong type and an error output is supplied.
identity.capability: Pass the member key to typed validation and include it in the diagnostic.
identity.consequence: The error cannot identify the member key.

obligations.requirement: An object-member type mismatch can report the expected and actual types together with the member key.

assessment.necessity_reason: For the selected unpack changes, a wrong typed object member can produce a key-qualified diagnostic when error output is supplied. The old harness supplies no unpack error output, and its fixed object formats contain no typed member validation.

before.requirement: The frozen key-qualified object-member type diagnostic was not supported; a type mismatch reported the expected and actual types without the member key.
before.reason: The object unpacker did not pass the member key to typed validation, and the type error text had no key qualifier.

after.requirement: For a keyed object member of the wrong expected type, an error-reporting unpack can include that member key in the type diagnostic.
after.reason: The object unpacker passes the key to typed validation, which includes it in the diagnostic. The old harness calls json_unpack, whose wrapper supplies a null error pointer; its object formats also use only the untyped 'o' extraction.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The public wrapper used by the harness passes a null error pointer to json_vunpack_ex.
The unpack entry forwards its error pointer into the scanner and starts validation.

assessment.comparison_reason: The same old harness has no route to the new key-qualified diagnostic. That specific diagnostic was not supported before the change.

necessity_evidence.reason: Object-member unpacking now supports a key-qualified wrong-type diagnostic when an error output is supplied. The fixed target's unpack formats use untyped extraction, and json_unpack supplies no error output. This specific coverage gap was introduced by the changed source contract.
necessity_evidence.finite_witness: Input bytes: 00 7b 22 62 61 72 22 3a 34 32 7d (prefix byte followed by {"bar":42}). The supported setup json_unpack_ex(root, &error, 0, "{ss}", "bar", &out) reports "Expected string, got integer for key bar"; the target cannot select that setup.

scope_contract.reason: The target's primary operation is object unpacking. Its format protocol supports keyed, typed member validation and an error-reporting unpack entry, so this diagnostic belongs to that operation's surface.

evidence.dependency_reason: The error-reporting public unpack entry forwards the supplied error output to json_vunpack_ex.

feasible_trigger.reason: A finite valid object and typed format trigger the supported diagnostic with an error output. The target can parse that object, but its fixed unpack calls cannot supply the required format and error output.

evidence.dependency_reason: The input suffix is parsed as JSON before the target's unpack calls.
These fixed calls determine the target's actual unpack setup.

observable_consequence.reason: The changed validator includes the member key in the error text, a behavior demonstrated by the supplied API test. The target exposes no unpack error text and cannot reach that diagnostic.

evidence.dependency_reason: The API test demonstrates the resulting key-qualified diagnostic.
The target's json_unpack wrapper always passes a null unpack error output.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: The complete target entry has only fixed untyped object formats and an array format. Input bytes change the JSON value, not those formats or the null unpack error output. The loader's error output concerns JSON parsing, not this object-member unpack diagnostic.

evidence.dependency_reason: The target's o format extracts a value without typed-member validation.
Every target json_unpack call forwards a null error output.
Array elements pass a null member key, so the array call is not an equivalent key-qualified route.

identity_preserved.reason: The same tuple is assessed on both versions: keyed object-member type mismatch with an error output. Before, the object unpacker did not forward the key and the type diagnostic omitted it; after, both include it. The old harness is fixed across that comparison.

evidence.dependency_reason: These are the fixed old-harness unpack calls used for both sides of the timing comparison.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The target's wrapper passes a null error output.

coverage_witness.supported_behavior: A keyed object-member type mismatch reports the expected type, actual type, and member key through an error-reporting unpack call.
coverage_witness.required_setup: Parse {"bar":42}; call json_unpack_ex with an error output and format "{ss}" for member "bar".
coverage_witness.actual_target_setup: The target parses the JSON suffix and calls json_unpack with fixed formats "o", "{s?o}", and "[o!]"; json_unpack forwards a null error output.
coverage_witness.blocked_behavior: The target cannot reach or expose "Expected string, got integer for key bar".
coverage_witness.equivalent_routes: None in the complete target entry: its object formats have no typed-member check, its array format supplies no member key, and its parse error output concerns a different operation.

identity.operation: Unpack a scalar using s, i, I, b, f, F, or n.
identity.condition: A type-specific scalar format is selected.
identity.capability: Validate and extract the corresponding JSON scalar type.
identity.consequence: Scalar extraction or type-mismatch rejection fails.

obligations.requirement: Unpack scalar values with type-specific format characters and reject mismatched JSON types.

assessment.necessity_reason: Typed scalar formats are supported by json_unpack on both sides. The complete old harness supplies only formats whose value token is o, so fuzz input cannot select typed scalar validation or extraction.

before.requirement: Allow json_unpack to select s, i, I, b, f, F, or n to validate a scalar type and extract a value where that format assigns one.
before.reason: The unpack implementation supports these formats, but all three fixed harness formats select o for their values. No input byte controls the format string.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The harness calls json_unpack, which forwards its fixed format to json_vunpack_ex.
json_vunpack_ex dispatches that format to unpack.

after.requirement: Allow json_unpack to select s, i, I, b, f, F, or n to validate a scalar type and extract a value where that format assigns one.
after.reason: The typed cases remain supported, while the same fixed harness still supplies only o as a value token.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The harness calls json_unpack, which forwards its fixed format to json_vunpack_ex.
json_vunpack_ex dispatches that format to unpack.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: Input bytes select a variant and JSON text; the entry does not derive an unpack format from them.

assessment.comparison_reason: The identical fixed-format constraint prevents the same typed-scalar operation on both source versions.

necessity_evidence.reason: Typed scalar unpacking is within json_unpack's format contract, but the fixed harness uses only o as a value token. The same blocker exists before and after the source change.
necessity_evidence.finite_witness: Input bytes 0x00 followed by {"data":"x"} produce an object with a string field. A supported setup could unpack that field with {s?s} and a string output pointer; the target instead uses {s?o}, regardless of the input bytes.

scope_contract.reason: The entry calls json_unpack. Its format contract includes typed scalar tokens and permits them within object unpacking.

evidence.dependency_reason: Object formats dispatch their value token to unpack.

feasible_trigger.reason: The finite input parses as an object with a string field. The source supports typed string extraction for that field, while the input controls JSON content but cannot select its unpack format.

evidence.dependency_reason: The object format supports a typed value token after its key.
Input supplies a selector byte and JSON text.

observable_consequence.reason: No input reaches typed scalar extraction or type-mismatch rejection through json_unpack: every target value token is o.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: The complete entry has only three fixed unpack calls. Their o tokens extract generic JSON values, including when the input contains a scalar; the other entry operations do not select a typed unpack format.

evidence.dependency_reason: The o case performs generic extraction, whereas n performs null validation.
The supplied format is dispatched to unpack without deriving another format from the JSON input.

identity_preserved.reason: Both source versions support the same typed scalar unpack operation, and the same fixed harness blocks its selection on both sides. The obligation is preexisting.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The public json_unpack call forwards its format and arguments.
The after-version public call forwards its format and arguments.

coverage_witness.supported_behavior: json_unpack validates a scalar against s, i, I, b, f, F, or n and extracts the value where that token assigns one.
coverage_witness.required_setup: Select a typed scalar value token with a matching output argument where required; for example, unpack the string field of {"data":"x"} using {s?s}.
coverage_witness.actual_target_setup: The entry selects only o, {s?o}, and [o!] as unpack formats.
coverage_witness.blocked_behavior: Typed scalar validation and extraction through json_unpack cannot be reached by any fuzzer input.
coverage_witness.equivalent_routes: None in the complete entry; JSON parsing and generic o extraction do not perform typed scalar unpacking.
